result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers index rent and regional prices to 2016 = 100, plot them together with direct end labels, and use a non-zero baseline. Neither one reports the roughly 12% real increase or gives values in 2016 dollars. A comes out ahead because its title puts both figures side by side (48% vs 33%), it says the rents are not inflation-adjusted, and it states that the axis starts at 100. B's title and big +$565 and +48% callouts lead with the nominal figure alone. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers index rent and the regional price index to 2016 = 100 and plot them as two lines. Neither shows an adjusted rent in 2016 dollars or states the roughly 12% real increase. B's title puts the 48% rent rise next to the 33% price rise, and its footnote says the rent figures are not adjusted for inflation and that the axis starts at 100, not zero. A's title gives only the 48% figure, its y-axis starts at 90 without any note, and its '2016 level' label overlaps the lines.
